title: Calibration loss on paired splits
question: What was the largest mean loss across test splits?
clean: The maximum of the two split means was 12. Individual losses were not saved.
flawed: The maximum individual loss across all samples was 12.
defect: Confuses a maximum of split means with an individual maximum that the data do not identify.

title: Masked covariates in regression
question: Does the comparison isolate the causal effect of retraining?
clean: The frozen and retrained models used different test distributions, so their error gap cannot identify a retraining effect.
flawed: The lower error proves that retraining causally improves prediction at fixed test distribution.
defect: The compared arms changed the test distribution along with retraining.

title: Paired sort timings
question: Did caching improve the median elapsed time in these paired trials?
clean: Caching showed no median benefit on the three paired trials. We make no population-level speedup claim.
flawed: Caching reduced median elapsed time by half across the three paired trials.
defect: Both sample medians are 10 ms. A well-scoped null result is supported.

title: What an archived study measured
question: Which parameter was selected by the cited study?
clean: The cited study selected the penalty on a validation set. Its observation does not establish test-set tuning.
flawed: The cited study selected the penalty using test labels.
source: The penalty was selected using validation labels. Test labels were hidden until evaluation.
defect: The original explicitly states validation labels were used, contradicting the attribution to test labels.

title: Predictive error after adding irrelevant coordinates
question: We evaluated the same five-neighbor regressor and paired test splits in two feature spaces. The recorded endpoints were test RMSE and MAE. What do these comparisons establish?
clean: Prediction error increased on all five splits with the irrelevant coordinates. Changes in the selected neighborhoods are a possible explanation.
flawed: Prediction error increased on all five splits with the irrelevant coordinates. The measurements establish that changes in the selected neighborhoods dominate the increase.
defect: The paired errors support the observed performance gap. The experiment records neither neighbor identities nor a decomposition of the error. Calling neighborhood changes the dominant cause exceeds the measurements. Limit the claim to a hypothesis or supply evidence that distinguishes its contribution.
